THOUGHT: Acute, unilateral painful red eye with marked visual loss in a regular contact lens wearer strongly suggests contact lens–associated infectious keratitis. Slit-lamp shows corneal ulceration with stromal infiltrate consistent with microbial keratitis. Corneal scraping culture grew Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a classic, rapidly progressive pathogen in contact lens–related corneal ulcers. Other causes (acute angle-closure glaucoma, sterile keratitis, viral dendritic keratitis) are less likely given the corneal infiltrate and positive bacterial culture. The history, exam, slit-lamp findings, and microbiology together confirm a bacterial corneal infection due to Pseudomonas. 
DIAGNOSIS: Contact lens–associated Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacterial keratitis (microbial corneal ulcer)
